Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with inner product linear in the first variable, and let $\mathcal F_-(H)$ be its fermionic Fock space. The creation rule $C(f)\xi=f\wedge\xi$ extends to a bounded operator on $\mathcal F_-(H)$ with $\|C(f)\|=\|f\|$. Writing $A(f)=C(f)^*$ for its adjoint, one has, for all $f,g\in H$,

$$ \{C(f),C(g)\}=0,\qquad \{A(f),A(g)\}=0,\qquad \{A(f),C(g)\}=\langle g,f\rangle I. $$

Thus $f\mapsto C(f)$ is a bounded complex-linear CAR family in the convention of [[def-finite-dimensional-car-algebra]].

space and let $A,B:H\to H$ be trace-class operators. Write $D_T$ for the

2. For every $z\in\mathbb C$,

let $T:H\to H$ be trace class. Write $\Lambda(T)=\{\lambda\in\sigma(T):

$m_{\mathrm{alg}}(\lambda;T)=\dim G_\lambda(T)$. Define
$$M:=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{G_\lambda(T):\lambda\in\Lambda(T)\}},\qquad P:=P_M,\qquad Q:=I-P,$$
where $P_M$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection onto $M$. Put
$T_M:=T|_M$ and $D:=(QTQ)|_{M^\perp}$. Then $T_M$ and $D$ are trace class,
and $D$ has no nonzero spectral values (the assertion is vacuous if

and the eigenvalue sum is absolutely convergent. The extension $QTQ:H\to H$
is quasinilpotent and has trace zero.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and
$T\in\mathcal S_1(H)$. The function $D_T(z)=\det_H(I+zT)$ is entire and,
locally uniformly in $z$,
$$
D_T(z)=\prod_j(1+z\lambda_j(T)),
$$
where all nonzero eigenvalues are listed with their finite algebraic
multiplicities, and $\sum_j|\lambda_j(T)|\leq\|T\|_1$. It satisfies
$$
D_T(0)=1,\qquad D_T'(0)=\operatorname{tr}_H(T),
$$
$$
|D_T(z)|\leq\prod_j(1+|z|s_j(T))\leq e^{|z|\|T\|_1},
$$
and for every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $C_\varepsilon$ such that
$|D_T(z)|\leq C_\varepsilon e^{\varepsilon|z|}$. For trace-class $A,B$,
$$ |D_A(z)-D_B(z)|\leq |z|\|A-B\|_1 e^{1+|z|\|A\|_1+|z|\|B\|_1}, $$
and
$$
\det_H(I+A+B+AB)=\det_H(I+A)\det_H(I+B).
$$
Moreover $D_T(z)=0$ exactly when $I+zT$ is not boundedly invertible, and the
zero at $-1/\lambda$ has the algebraic multiplicity of $\lambda\neq0$.

If finite-rank $T_n$ converge to $T$ in trace norm, their ordinary
finite-dimensional determinants converge to $D_T$ locally uniformly. Where
$I+zT$ is invertible,
$$
D_T'(z)=D_T(z)\operatorname{tr}_H\bigl(T(I+zT)^{-1}\bigr).
$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $\mathsf{CAR}(H)$ be the completion of its directed union of finite-dimensional CAR algebras from [[def-car-algebra-over-hilbert-space]]. Let $K\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space, and let $C:H\to\mathcal B(K)$ be a complex-linear family of bounded operators satisfying

$$ \{C(f),C(g)\}=0,\qquad \{C(f)^*,C(g)^*\}=0,\qquad \{C(f)^*,C(g)\}=\langle g,f\rangle I_K \quad(f,g\in H). $$

There is a unique unital isometric $*$-homomorphism $\rho:\mathsf{CAR}(H)\to\mathcal B(K)$ with $\rho(c(f))=C(f)$. For each $x$ in the algebraic union, its inductive-limit norm equals the supremum of $\|\rho(x)\|$ over all such families on nonzero Hilbert spaces. This family is nonempty: the fermionic Fock representation $C(f)\mapsto C(f)$ of [[lem-fock-creation-annihilation-satisfy-car]] attains the norm on every finite stage.

[F4] Fock creation operators and their adjoints satisfy the stated CAR relations ([[lem-fock-creation-annihilation-satisfy-car]]).

[F5] If $Y$ is Banach, then $\mathcal B(X,Y)$ is Banach for the operator norm ([[thm-bounded-operator-space-is-banach]]).

[F6] $\mathcal B(K)$ denotes bounded linear operators with operator norm $\|T\|=\sup_{\|x\|\le1}\|Tx\|$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]], [[def-operator-norm]]).
